title: Winter — I. Allegro non molto
rationale: A seasonal opening that paints winter in sound.
listenFor: Listen for shivering strings, icy winds and stamping feet.

title: Étude Op. 10 No. 12 — Revolutionary
rationale: Chopin turns a technical exercise into a furious musical drama.
listenFor: Follow the relentless left hand beneath the melody.

title: String Quartet in F major — II. Assez vif
rationale: Four musicians create an astonishingly rhythmic soundscape.
listenFor: Notice the contrast between plucked and bowed strings.

title: The Planets — Mars, the Bringer of War
performer: Charles Dutoit; Orchestre symphonique de Montréal
rationale: A dramatic orchestral work that anticipates modern film music.
listenFor: Try counting the repeating five-beat rhythm.

title: Má vlast — Vltava (The Moldau)
rationale: An entire landscape painted in music, following a river through Bohemia.
listenFor: Hear two small streams merge into a flowing river theme.

title: O virtus sapientiae
performer: Libby Crabtree, Ruth Dean, Anne Lewis, Rebecca Taverner and William Taylor
rationale: Music from nearly 900 years ago, with a very different musical language.
listenFor: Notice the flowing vocal line and absence of familiar chord progressions.

title: The Marriage of Figaro — Overture
performer: Sir Colin Davis; BBC Symphony Orchestra
rationale: Mozart captures excitement and comedy without a single word.
listenFor: Listen to little musical ideas darting between instruments.

title: La cathédrale engloutie (The Sunken Cathedral)
rationale: A piano becomes an ocean, a cathedral and a set of ringing bells.
listenFor: Imagine the cathedral rising and sinking as the sound changes.

title: Cello Suite No. 1 — Prelude
rationale: One instrument suggests an entire world of harmony.
listenFor: Listen for the chords implied by the flowing single notes.

title: Cotton Dance
rationale: An American composer brings together classical piano writing and African-American musical traditions.
listenFor: Notice the dance rhythms and playful accents.

title: Romeo and Juliet — Dance of the Knights
rationale: An imposing scene built from rhythm and orchestral colour.
listenFor: Notice how the heavy theme contrasts with the lighter middle section.

title: Piano Concerto No. 2 — II. Adagio sostenuto
performer: Vladimir Ashkenazy; André Previn; London Symphony Orchestra
rationale: A great Romantic concerto where the piano is not always the star.
listenFor: Listen to the piano accompany the woodwind melody.

title: Gianni Schicchi — O mio babbino caro
performer: Maria Callas; Tullio Serafin; Philharmonia Orchestra
rationale: An introduction to opera and the expressive power of the human voice.
listenFor: Even without Italian, listen for the pleading character of the melody.

title: Danse macabre
rationale: A spooky musical story about skeletons dancing at midnight.
listenFor: Listen for the xylophone imitating rattling bones.

title: Rain Tree Sketch II
rationale: Japanese contemporary piano music where silence matters as much as sound.
listenFor: Listen to notes fading away and the spaces between gestures.

title: Symphony No. 7 — II. Allegretto
rationale: A tiny rhythmic idea grows into something extraordinarily powerful.
listenFor: Follow the repeating rhythm as more instruments join it.

title: Libertango
rationale: Argentinian tango meets classical chamber music.
listenFor: Listen to syncopation and the tension between melody and pulse.

title: On an Overgrown Path — Good Night!
rationale: A small piano piece that says a great deal without flashy virtuosity.
listenFor: Notice the repeated gestures and changes in mood.

title: The Lark Ascending
performer: James Ehnes; Andrew Manze; Royal Liverpool Philharmonic Orchestra
rationale: A Canadian violinist performs a beautiful portrait of a bird in flight.
listenFor: Hear the solo violin float above the orchestra.

title: The Unanswered Question
rationale: Three musical groups seem to inhabit different worlds.
listenFor: The trumpet asks a question and the woodwinds struggle to answer over quiet strings.

title: Brandenburg Concerto No. 3 — I.
rationale: An exhilarating demonstration of musical conversation and counterpoint.
listenFor: Follow a short musical idea as it passes between instruments.

title: The Firebird Suite — Berceuse and Finale
rationale: A quiet lullaby grows into a spectacular orchestral climax.
listenFor: Listen for the horn melody and its increasingly triumphant orchestration.

title: The Nutcracker — Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairy
rationale: A Christmas classic introduces a keyboard instrument called the celesta.
listenFor: Compare its bell-like sound with the familiar piano.

title: Inception — Time
performer: Hans Zimmer — original motion picture soundtrack
rationale: A finale that connects the classical tradition to modern film music, showing how a simple musical idea can grow into something monumental. A little preview of the music you will experience when you see Hans Zimmer live.
listenFor: Listen to the quiet piano and repeating chord progression. Notice how new layers, changing dynamics and orchestral textures gradually transform the same musical idea, before the music returns to its intimate beginnings.
